history.content: Pitfalls: If the shape were actually L-shaped, there would be an inward step somewhere (e.g., a missing rectangular piece). If any small purple labels correspond to parts of an indentation (like 1 and 3 indicating notch width/height), they would reduce area from 42. Without such an indentation, 42 stands.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: General reference: For orthogonal polygons, area can be computed by decomposing into rectangles or by subtracting any notches from the bounding rectangle. If the outline is truly a full rectangle of 7×6, area is 42. If there is an inset notch (e.g., 1×3), the area would be 42−3=39. Confirm the boundary carefully.

mistake_reason: At step 3, FileSurfer reported the shape as a simple 7×6 rectangle and withheld critical boundary details: an inward notch near the top-right with small purple labels (e.g., dimensions 1 and 3) that reduce the area from 42 to 39. By concealing the concavity and specific small segment labels when asked to provide all visible side lengths and shape features, FileSurfer failed to share essential information needed by the team. This information withholding (FM-2.4) caused the Assistant to compute the area as the full rectangle (42) instead of subtracting the notch area, leading to the wrong answer.
